examples.dm: Whoever, as a protector, practices this perfection of wisdom, And whoever holds and masters it with devotion, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water; Mara and the factions of Mara will find no opportunity to harm them.
examples.gm: The perfection of wisdom, in which the Protectors practice— Whoever respects, apprehends, and masters it, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water, And Māra and the factions of Māra will find no opportunity against them.
examples.sa: य इमां ग्रहीष्यति पर्यापुणती स नित्यं प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति नाथाः । विष वह्नि शस्त्र उदकं न क्रमाति तस्यो ओतारु मारु न च विन्दति मारपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the Arhats, The suchness of the Pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the Bodhisattvas— These are a single suchness, devoid of entities, a non-dual suchness; The Tathāgata knows this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the arhats, The suchness of the pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the sons of the Victors: Are oneness, devoid of entities, not other; they are suchness; The perfection of wisdom is known by the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: लोकस्य या तथत या तथतार्हतानां । प्रत्येकबुद्धतथता तथता जिनानाम् । एकैव भावविगता तथता अनन्या प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुद्ध तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Those who possess such qualities are free from conceptual elaboration; Free from doubt, hesitation, and uncertainty, they are endowed with the true meaning. Having heard the perfection of wisdom, they do not shrink back; They do not rely on others and should be known as irreversible.
examples.gm: They are endowed with such dharmas and are free from conceptual proliferation. They are free from doubt, hesitation, and wavering, and possess the ultimate meaning. Those who, having heard the perfection of wisdom, do not shrink back, Should be known as irreversible and not reliant on others.
examples.sa: ते एव धर्मसमुदागत निष्प्रपञ्चा काङ्क्षाविलेखविमतीविगतार्थयुक्ताः । प्रज्ञाय पारमित श्रुत्व न सीदयन्ति अपरप्रणेय अविवर्तिय वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: Having abandoned both the arising and the complete passing away of all things, As many as are expressed by names throughout the worlds, One attains that supreme, deathless primordial wisdom, beyond which there is no other; For that reason, this is called the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: However many names of dharmas are proclaimed in the world, Having abandoned arising and passing away regarding all of them, One attains the supreme, deathless pristine wisdom, than which there is no other; Therefore, this is called the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यावन्ति लोकि परिकीर्तित धर्मनाम सर्वेषु पादसमतिक्रमु निर्गमित्वा । अमृतं ति ज्ञानु परमं न तु यो परेण एकार्थ प्रज्ञ अयु पारमितेति नामा ॥

examples.dm: Just as when the solar orb radiates its web of light, Sentient beings then apply themselves diligently to their tasks, So too, when the mind of enlightenment arises in the world for the sake of the wisdom of the sages, Through primordial wisdom, sentient beings come to possess the qualities of the Dharma.
examples.gm: When the sun's disk emits its web of light, At that time beings exert themselves in doing their work; likewise, When the mind of awakening emerges in the world for the sake of the knowledge of the wise, Through pristine knowledge beings become endowed with virtuous dharmas.
examples.sa: आदित्यमण्डलु यदा प्रभजाल मुञ्ची कर्मक्रियासु तद सत्त्व पराक्रमन्ति । तथ बोधिचित्त सद लोकविदुस्य ज्ञातो ज्ञानेन सर्वगुणधर्म समागमन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, while dwelling in emptiness, Abides without a fixed place, having perfected gnosis and miraculous powers; They display an infinite variety of activities for the sake of sentient beings, And for ten million eons, they feel no weariness or exhaustion.
examples.gm: Likewise, a skilled bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness, Having reached the other shore of pristine wisdom and miracles, does not dwell there, Demonstrates infinite kinds of activities to wanderers; For ten million aeons they have no weariness and no fatigue.
examples.sa: एमेव शून्यतस्थितो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञानर्द्धिपारमिगतो अनिकेतचारी । विविधां क्रियां जगति दर्शयते अनन्तां न च भज्यती न पि च खिद्यति कल्पकोटी ॥

examples.dm: One who knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not treat the illusion as one thing and the aggregates as another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in total peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever here knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion, And does not make illusion one thing and the aggregates another, Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in perfect peace— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: मायोपमां य इह जानति पञ्च स्कन्धां न च माय अन्य न च स्कन्ध करोति अन्यान् । नानात्वसंज्ञविगतो उपशान्तचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, having heard that these phenomena are like emanations and illusions, Is without doubt and repeatedly practices the training, Know that such a person has long since entered the Mahayana, And has performed service to many tens of billions of Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whoever, having heard that these dharmas are like emanations and illusions, Without doubt, trains and continuously applies themselves, That being should be known to have entered the Great Vehicle long ago, And to have served many tens of millions of billions of Buddhas.
examples.sa: चिरयानप्रस्थितु स वेदयितव्य सत्त्वो बहुबुद्धकोटिनयुतेहि कृताधिकारो । यो श्रुत्व धर्मि इमि निर्मितमायकल्पां न च काङ्क्षते अयु प्रयुज्यति शिक्षमाणः ॥

examples.dm: In the midst of a crowd, a conjured person does not think, "I must please these people," and yet they perform that very action; Although they are seen displaying various miraculous feats, They possess no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.gm: In the midst of people, an illusory person does not think, "I will please these people," yet still pleases them; Though seen to display various miracles, They have no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.sa: यथ मायकारपुरुषस्य न एव भोति ते शिष्य मां जनत सो च करोति कार्यम् । पश्यन्ति तं विविध कार्यु निदर्शयन्तं न च तस्य कायु न पि चित्त न नामधेयम् ॥

examples.dm: Form is not wisdom, and wisdom is not found within form. Consciousness, perception, feeling, and intention— These are not wisdom, nor is wisdom present within them. This is identical to the element of space, without any distinction.
examples.gm: Form is not wisdom, in form there is no wisdom; Consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition—these Are not wisdom, nor is there wisdom in these; This is equal to the realm of space, without difference.
examples.sa: रुपे न प्रज्ञ इति रुपि न अस्ति प्रज्ञा विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च । न च एति प्रज्ञ इति तेष न अस्ति प्रज्ञा आकाशधातुसम तस्य न चास्ति भेदः ॥

examples.dm: One should understand that the purity of form is the purity of the fruition; The purity of the fruition and the purity of form become the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruition, and the purity of form Are like the element of space—indivisible and inseparable.
examples.gm: The purity of form should be known as the purity of the fruit; The purity of the fruit and form becomes the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruit, and the purity of form Are equal to the realm of space, indivisible and unseverable.
examples.sa: रूपस्य शुद्धि फलशुद्धित वेदितव्या फलरूपशुद्धित सर्वज्ञतशुद्धिम् आहुः । सर्वज्ञताय फलशुद्धित रूपशुद्धी आकाशधातुसमताय अभिन्नछिन्नाः ॥

examples.dm: Wind relies upon space, and the mass of water relies upon that. This great earth relies upon that, and living beings rely upon it. Such is the causal basis for sentient beings' engagement in karma; Reflect on the meaning of this: upon what does space abide?
examples.gm: Wind is supported on space, on that is supported the mass of water, On that is supported this great earth, on that are supported living beings; Such is the cause of sentient beings engaging in karma; Think about this meaning of space being a pervasive foundation!
examples.sa: आकाशनिश्रित समीरण आपस्कन्धो त हि निश्रिता इह महापृथिवी जगच्च । सत्त्वान कर्म-उपभोगनिदानम् एव आकाशस्थानु कुतु चिन्तयि एतम् अर्थम् ॥

examples.dm: Form is not wisdom, and wisdom is not found within form. Consciousness, perception, feeling, and intention— These are not wisdom, nor is wisdom present within them. This is identical to the element of space, without any distinction.
examples.gm: Form is not wisdom, in form there is no wisdom; Consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition—these Are not wisdom, nor is there wisdom in these; This is equal to the realm of space, without difference.
examples.sa: रुपे न प्रज्ञ इति रुपि न अस्ति प्रज्ञा विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च । न च एति प्रज्ञ इति तेष न अस्ति प्रज्ञा आकाशधातुसम तस्य न चास्ति भेदः ॥

examples.dm: The nature of all objective referents is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless. The nature of the expanse of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.gm: The nature of objects of apprehension is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless; The nature of the realm of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.sa: आरम्बणान प्रकृती स अ(न)न्तपारा सत्त्वान या च प्रकृती स अनन्तपारा । आकाशधातुप्रकृती स अनन्तपारा प्रज्ञा पि लोकविदुनां स अनन्तपारा ॥

examples.dm: The element of space in the eastern direction and the southern direction, And likewise in the western direction and the northern direction, is infinite; It exists above, below, and in all the ten directions as far as they extend. It is without differentiation and without any distinctions.
examples.gm: The element of space in the eastern direction and the southern direction, And likewise in the western direction and the northern direction, is boundless; Above, below, and in as many of the ten directions as there are, it exists; There is no difference and there is no distinction.
examples.sa: आकाशधातु पुरिमादिशि दक्षिणायां तथ पश्चिमोत्तरदिशाय अनन्तपारा । उपराधराय दशद्दिशि यावदस्ति नानात्वता न भवते न विशेषप्राप्ता ॥

examples.dm: If one gives rise to the perception of sentient beings or the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes a self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: If they generate the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," They are a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि सत्त्वसंज्ञ दुखसंज्ञ उपादयाती हरिष्यामि दुःख जगतीं करिष्यामि अर्थम् । सो आत्मस(त्त्व) परिकल्पकु बोधिसत्त्वो न च एष प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Know that all sentient beings are exactly as oneself is; Know that all phenomena are exactly as all sentient beings are; Not conceptualizing either non-arising or arising— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Knowing all sentient beings to be like oneself, Knowing all dharmas to be like all sentient beings, Not conceptualizing both non-arising and arising, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ आत्मनं तथ प्रजानति सर्वसत्त्वां यथ सर्वसत्त्व तथ प्रजानति सर्वधर्मान् । अनुपादुपादु उभये अविकल्पमानो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: When writing down this Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Various and diverse kinds of flashes of inspiration will arise; Yet if, without having benefited sentient beings, they vanish as swiftly as lightning, This complete deterioration is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: When copying this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Various differing modes of confidence will arise; Yet without accomplishing the benefit of beings, swiftly like lightning, They will completely fade away; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: प्रतिभान नेक विविधानि उपपद्यिष्यन्ति लिखमान प्रज्ञ इमु पारमिता जिनानाम् । युत शीघ्र विद्युत यथा परिहायिष्यन्ति अकरित्व अर्थ जगती इमु मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: At that time, these activities of Māra will occur. At that time, after many monks have been stirred to agitation, Many other various obstacles will also arise, Which prevent them from upholding this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: At that time, this work of Māra will arise: At that time, whoever disturbs many monks, They will not uphold this perfection of wisdom; And many other various obstacles will also arise.
examples.sa: इमि मारकर्म भविष्यन्ति य तस्मि काले अन्ये च नेक विविधा बहु अन्तराया । येही समाकुलिकृता बहु भिक्षु तत्र प्रज्ञाय पारमित एतु न धारयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: When this is explained, some will harbor doubts, thinking: "The Leader has not even mentioned my name here; He has not mentioned my family, my level, or my lineage." This is the work of Māra, causing them to reject it rather than listen.
examples.gm: When this is taught, some will harbor doubts, thinking, 'The Leader has not fully pronounced my name here, Nor fully pronounced my lineage, birthplace, or clan.' They will not listen and will abandon it; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: काङ्क्षा च केषचि भविष्यति भाषमाणे न ममात्र नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन । न च जाति भूमि परिकीर्तितु नापि गोत्रं न च सो श्रुणिष्यति क्षिपिष्यति मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Possessing great generosity, great intelligence, and great power, They have entered the supreme Great Vehicle of the Victors; Clad in great armor, they subdue the illusions of Māra; For that reason, they are truly called "great beings."
examples.gm: Great giving, great intelligence, and great power, Entering into the supreme Great Vehicle of the Jinas, Donning the great armor and subduing the illusions of Mara; Therefore they are proclaimed to be a "great being."
examples.sa: महनायको महतबुद्धि महानुभावो महयान उत्तमजिनान समाधिरूढो । महता सनद्धु नमुचिं शठ धर्षयिष्ये महसत्त्व तेन हि प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, having heard that these phenomena are like emanations and illusions, Is without doubt and repeatedly practices the training, Know that such a person has long since entered the Mahayana, And has performed service to many tens of billions of Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whoever, having heard that these dharmas are like emanations and illusions, Without doubt, trains and continuously applies themselves, That being should be known to have entered the Great Vehicle long ago, And to have served many tens of millions of billions of Buddhas.
examples.sa: चिरयानप्रस्थितु स वेदयितव्य सत्त्वो बहुबुद्धकोटिनयुतेहि कृताधिकारो । यो श्रुत्व धर्मि इमि निर्मितमायकल्पां न च काङ्क्षते अयु प्रयुज्यति शिक्षमाणः ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening?" It is because by mounting it, one delivers all sentient beings from suffering. This vehicle is a vast celestial palace, as immense as space; It is the supreme vehicle, the means for fully attaining joy, delight, and bliss.
examples.gm: Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening? Mounting it, all sentient beings pass beyond sorrow. This vehicle is a great immeasurable palace like space, The supreme vehicle, which brings about the attainment of joy, happiness, and bliss.
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधियानो यत्रारुहित्व स निर्वापयि सर्वसत्त्वान् । आकाशतुल्य अयु यान महाविमानो सुखसौख्यक्षेमभिप्रापणु यानश्रेष्ठो ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: If one dedicates merit to enlightenment in this way, One is "poison-free," does not forsake the Buddha, and speaks what the Victors have taught. The hero who dedicates in this way outshines All those bodhisattvas in the world who engage in conceptual apprehension.
examples.gm: If one perfectly dedicates merit to awakening in that way, It is without poison, one does not abandon the Buddha, and speaks what the Victor has spoken. Dedicating perfectly in that way, the hero outshines all Of however many bodhisattvas there are in the world who possess apprehension.
examples.sa: एवं च पुण्य परिणामयमान बोधौ न च सो हि बुद्ध क्षिपते जिन उक्तवादी । यावन्ति लोकि उपलम्भिकबोधिसत्त्वा अभिभोन्ति सर्वि परिणामयमान शूरो ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥

examples.dm: The fifth chapter explains the clear realization of the pinnacle. One who does not desire the level of an Arhat, the wisdom of a Pratyekabuddha, Or the three realms, even in a dream, But sees the Buddhas and teaches the Dharma to beings— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: Chapter Five: Teaching the Clear Realization of the Peak. The stage of an arhat and the pristine wisdom of a pratyekabuddha, And the three realms, they do not desire even in dreams; Seeing the buddhas and teaching the dharma to wanderers, They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: अर्हन्तभूमिम् अपि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमौ त्रैधातुकं न स्पृशते सुपिनान्तरेऽपि । बुद्धांश् च पश्यति कथेति जनस्य धर्मं अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: If, in a dream, one sees sentient beings dwelling in the three lower realms, And in that very moment makes a prayer to cut the continuum of the lower realms, And pacifies a mass of fire through the power of the blessing of truth— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In a dream, seeing sentient beings abiding in the three lower realms, In that instant they make aspirations to cut off the stream of the lower realms. Through the blessing of truth, the masses of fire are pacified; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: त्रि-अपायप्राप्तु सुपिनस्मि विदित्व सत्त्वान् प्रणिधेति तत्क्षण अपाय उच्छोषयेयम् । सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति स चाग्निस्कन्धम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: भूतग्रहा विविध व्याधय मर्त्यलोके सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति हितानुकम्पी । न च तेन मन्यन् उपपद्यति नापि मानम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यः ॥

examples.dm: Form, perception, feeling, intention, And consciousness are neither bound nor freed, and they do not exist. Thus, entering into awakening without a discouraged mind, This is the supreme armor of holy beings.
examples.gm: Form and perception, feeling and volition, And consciousness are not bound, not liberated, and do not exist. Entering into awakening in this way, without a discouraged mind, This is the supreme armor of the noble persons.
examples.sa: रुपं च संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान बन्धु न च मुक्त असङ्गभूतो । एवं च बोधि क्रमते न च लीनचित्तो संना ह एष वरपुद्गल-उत्तमानाम् ॥

examples.dm: In which form is not apprehended, nor feeling, nor perception, Nor consciousness, nor intention is apprehended, And all phenomena are thoroughly known to be unborn and empty— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Where form is not, feeling is not, and perception is not apprehended, Consciousness is not, and volition is not apprehended, And all dharmas are fully known in the manner of being unarisen and empty: This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिन् न रूप अपि वेदन चापि संज्ञा विज्ञान नैव न पि चेतनयोपलब्धिः । अनुपादु शून्य न य जानति सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The wise and learned Bodhisattva who practices in this way, Does not train in the stage of an Arhat, nor in the stage of a Pratyekabuddha; For the sake of omniscience, they train following the Buddha-dharma. One who does not train in the distinction between training and non-training is one who trains.
examples.gm: A wise, understanding bodhisattva who practices in this way Does not train for the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha; For the sake of omniscience itself, they train in the qualities of a buddha; Whoever does not train in training and no-more-training, that is training.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो नार्हंमि शिक्षति न प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमौ । सर्वज्ञताय अनुशिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे शिक्षाअशिक्ष न य शिक्षति एष शिक्षा ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, when seeking complete awakening, those who get to hear This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Will find relief and become fearless; This is not the level of an Arhat, nor the level of a Pratyekabuddha.
examples.gm: Likewise, when seeking enlightenment, whoever attains the hearing Of this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, They attain relief and become fearless— Not of the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमिता जिनानां शृणु तात यो लभति बोधि गवेषमाणः । आश्वासप्राप्त भवती न च तस्य त्रासो नार्हन्तभूमि न पि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमी ॥

examples.dm: If no sprout exists, a tree could never grow in the world; In that case, how could branches, flowers, and fruit ever appear? If the mind of enlightenment did not exist, no Victors would ever arise in the world; And if so, how could the fruits—Indra, Brahmā, and the Hearers—ever appear?
examples.gm: If the emergence of a tree in the world never happens without a sprout, How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits emerge on it? If the emergence of a Victor in the world does not exist without the mind of awakening, How could the fruits of Śakra, Brahmā, and śrāvakas emerge?
examples.sa: असतोऽङ्कुरस्य द्रुमसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शाखपत्रफलपुष्पौपादु तत्र । विन बोधिचित्त जिनसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शक्रब्रह्मफल श्रावकप्रादुभावः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, when seeking complete awakening, those who get to hear This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Will find relief and become fearless; This is not the level of an Arhat, nor the level of a Pratyekabuddha.
examples.gm: Likewise, when seeking enlightenment, whoever attains the hearing Of this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, They attain relief and become fearless— Not of the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमिता जिनानां शृणु तात यो लभति बोधि गवेषमाणः । आश्वासप्राप्त भवती न च तस्य त्रासो नार्हन्तभूमि न पि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमी ॥

examples.dm: At that time, these activities of Māra will occur. At that time, after many monks have been stirred to agitation, Many other various obstacles will also arise, Which prevent them from upholding this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: At that time, this work of Māra will arise: At that time, whoever disturbs many monks, They will not uphold this perfection of wisdom; And many other various obstacles will also arise.
examples.sa: इमि मारकर्म भविष्यन्ति य तस्मि काले अन्ये च नेक विविधा बहु अन्तराया । येही समाकुलिकृता बहु भिक्षु तत्र प्रज्ञाय पारमित एतु न धारयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles Might remain in the sky and simultaneously display various transformations; He demonstrates walking, moving, lying down, and sitting, And he does not grow weary, nor does he become exhausted.
examples.gm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles, Abiding in space, simultaneously emanates magical creations, Demonstrating walking, pacing, sleeping, and sitting; He has no weariness, and he has no fatigue.
examples.sa: भिक्षू यथा परमऋद्धिबलेनुपेतो गगने स्थितो यमक कुर्वति प्रातिहार्यां । गतिचंक्रमं शयनिषद्य निदर्शयाति न निवर्तते न पि च खिद्यति याव तत्र ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the skillful bodhisattva also, Generates great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, And having completely transcended the four Māras and even the two levels, Abides in supreme meditative absorption, yet does not touch upon awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, at that time, a skilled bodhisattva, Generating great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, Having utterly passed beyond the four māras and the two, Dwells in the supreme samādhi and does not touch awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव यस्मि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो महमैत्रि सर्वि उपबन्धति सत्त्वधातौ । चतुरो स मार अतिक्रम्य द्वये च भूमिम् अस्मिन् समाधि स्थितु नो च स्पृशाति बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Through four causes, the wise and powerful bodhisattva Is difficult for the four Māras to overcome and cannot be shaken: Abiding in emptiness, never forsaking sentient beings, Acting exactly as one speaks, and possessing the blessings of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: By four causes, the wise bodhisattva possesses strength, Is hard to overcome by the four Māras, and cannot be moved: Dwelling in emptiness, not forsaking sentient beings, Acting as they have spoken, and possessing the blessing of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: चतुकारणेहि बलवां विदु बोधिसत्त्वो भवते दुघर्षु चतुमारअसंप्रकम्प्यो । शून्याविहारि भवते न च सत्त्वत्यागी यथवादि सत्त्वकरुणानुगतावस्थानः ॥

examples.dm: For example, it is like being stricken by poison through the mere perception of suspicion; Even if that poison has not entered the body, one will fall unconscious. Likewise, the childish who claim "I" and "mine," Have the notion of a self, and through unreal conceptualization, are born and die in impermanence.
examples.gm: For example, just as poison aroused by the perception of suspicion, Even if that poison has not gone inside, one will faint; Likewise, childish beings, accepting self and what belongs to self, Perceiving that self, which is not real, constantly are born and die.
examples.sa: यथ शङ्कितेन विषसंज्ञत अभ्युपैति नो चास्य कोष्ठगतु सो विषु पात्यते च । एमेव बालुपगतो अहु मह्य एषो अहसंज्ञि जायि म्रियते च सदा अभूतो ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: Through ethical discipline, those who desire peace become noble. Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their ethical discipline never declines. They follow all the various activities of the vows; For the benefit of all beings, they also dedicate them to enlightenment.
examples.gm: Through discipline, those who desire peace become exalted; Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their discipline does not wane. They engage in all the activities of vows, whatever they may be, And dedicate them to awakening for the benefit of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: शीलेन उद्गत भवन्ति समाधिकाङ्क्षी स्थित गोचरे दशबलान अखण्डशीलाः । यावन्ति संवरक्रिय अनुवर्तयन्ति तां सर्वसत्त्वहित बोधयि नामयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: Then, in order to cause those four assemblies to be perfectly and thoroughly delighted, the Blessed One taught this perfection of wisdom once more, and at that time spoke these verses:
examples.gm: Then, in order to perfectly delight those four assemblies, the Blessed One once again taught this perfection of wisdom and at that time spoke these verses.
examples.sa: अथ खलु भगवांस् तासां चतसृणां पर्षदां संप्रहर्षणार्थं पुनरपीमां प्रज्ञापारमितां परिदीपयमानस् तस्यां वेलायामिमा गाथा अभाषत -

examples.dm: Those who possess spiritual friends and possess special insight, Will never become afraid upon hearing the Mother of the Victors. Those who associate with negative friends and rely on others, Are like an unfired clay vessel that disintegrates when touched by water.
examples.gm: Possessing spiritual friends and possessing profound insight, Hearing the Mother of the Jinas, they will not be afraid. Whoever possesses bad friends and depends upon others, Is like an unfired clay vessel that collapses when it contacts water.
examples.sa: कल्याणमित्रसहितस्य विपश्यकस्य त्रासो न भेष्यति श्रुणित्व जिनान मात्राम् । यो पापमित्रसहितो च परप्रणेयो सो आमभाजन यथोदकस्पृष्ट भिन्नो ॥

examples.dm: If one gives rise to the perception of sentient beings or the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes a self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: If they generate the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," They are a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि सत्त्वसंज्ञ दुखसंज्ञ उपादयाती हरिष्यामि दुःख जगतीं करिष्यामि अर्थम् । सो आत्मस(त्त्व) परिकल्पकु बोधिसत्त्वो न च एष प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: It is not for the sake of the increase, decrease, or grasping of form; Nor is it for the sake of grasping the various phenomena that one trains. While training, one also grasps omniscience itself; This very transcendence is the training of those who delight in excellence.
examples.gm: It is not for the sake of the increase, complete deterioration, or complete apprehension of form; Not training for the sake of completely apprehending various dharmas, Yet training and completely apprehending omniscience itself— Whatever definite emergence this is, this is the training that rejoices in qualities.
examples.sa: न च रुपवृद्धिपरिहाणिपरिग्रहाये न च शिक्षति विविधधर्मपरिग्रहाये । सर्वज्ञतां च परिगृह्णति शिक्षमाणो निर्यायती य इय शिक्ष गुणे रतानाम् ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Here demonstrate that all phenomena are emptiness. Having heard that, the Hearers quickly reach liberation, And they reach the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Buddhas.
examples.gm: If asked why: those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Demonstrate all dharmas here as emptiness. Hearing that, śrāvakas swiftly touch complete liberation, And touch the awakening of pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of buddhas.
examples.sa: किं कारणं त इह शिक्षित वादिश्रेष्ठा गमयन्ति धर्म निखिलानिह शून्यतायाम् । यां श्रुत्व श्रावक स्पृशन्ति विमुक्ति शीघ्रं प्रत्येकबोधि स्पृशयन्ति च बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: One should understand that the purity of form is the purity of the fruition; The purity of the fruition and the purity of form become the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruition, and the purity of form Are like the element of space—indivisible and inseparable.
examples.gm: The purity of form should be known as the purity of the fruit; The purity of the fruit and form becomes the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruit, and the purity of form Are equal to the realm of space, indivisible and unseverable.
examples.sa: रूपस्य शुद्धि फलशुद्धित वेदितव्या फलरूपशुद्धित सर्वज्ञतशुद्धिम् आहुः । सर्वज्ञताय फलशुद्धित रूपशुद्धी आकाशधातुसमताय अभिन्नछिन्नाः ॥

examples.dm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the Buddha-qualities, Nor do they conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, awakening, or peace. They practice through the blessing of non-conceptuality, free from mental construction; This is the practice of the supreme Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the qualities of a Buddha; They do not conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, or peaceful enlightenment; Non-conceptualizing and free from concepts, they practice through blessing; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु यो न इह कल्पयि बुद्धधर्मां बल ऋद्धिपाद न च कल्पयि बोधि शान्ताम् । अविकल्पकल्पविगतोऽधिष्ठानचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: For those small-minded beings who have newly entered the vehicle, If they have not attained this rare and precious jewel, Mara will strive to create obstacles for them; The Buddhas of the ten directions apply themselves to protecting them.
examples.gm: Sentient beings of small intellect who have newly entered the vehicle, Who have not found this rare jewel— In order to create obstacles for them, Māra will become energetic; But the Buddhas of the ten directions will apply themselves to fully protecting them.
examples.sa: नवयानप्रस्थित स सत्त्व परीत्तबुद्धिः य इमं दुर्लाभु धर्मरतनं परापुणन्ति । मारोऽत्र उत्सुकु भविष्यति अन्तराये बुद्धा दशद्दिशि परिग्रहसंप्रयुक्ताः ॥

examples.dm: One does not see forms, nor does one see feelings, One does not see perceptions, nor does one see intentions, That in which consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata taught that this is "seeing the Dharma."
examples.gm: Not seeing forms, and also not seeing feelings, Not seeing perceptions, and not seeing formations, For whom consciousness, mind, and intellect are not seen— The Tathāgata has taught that this is seeing the dharma.
examples.sa: रूपस्य दर्शनु अदर्शनु वेदनाये संज्ञाय दर्शनु अदर्शनु चेतनाये । विज्ञानचित्तमनुदर्शनु यत्र नास्ति अय धर्मदर्शनु निदिष्टु तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.
examples.gm: Practicing thus, those oceans of goodness, moons of speech, Are the refuge, the defender, and the resting place of beings; They are the support, the mind, the island, and the supreme guides seeking their welfare; They are illuminating lamps, speakers of the supreme dharma, and are unperturbed.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.dm: Sentient beings delight in foundations and desire sense objects; Abiding in grasping, they are unskilled, foolish, and deluded like darkness. The phenomena to be attained are without foundation and without grasping; Therefore, conflict with the world arises.
examples.gm: Beings delight in resting places and desire sense objects; Abiding in grasping, the unwise are foolish and obscured like darkness. The dharma to be attained is without resting place and without grasping; Therefore, conflict arises with the worlds.
examples.sa: सत्त्वश् च आलयरतो विषयाभिलाषी स्थित अग्रहे अबुध यो महअन्धभूतो । धर्मो अनालयु अनाग्रहु प्रापितव्यो लोकेन सार्ध अयु विग्रहु प्रादुभूतो ॥

examples.dm: Pure and wearing clean robes, they are pure in the three isolations; They do not desire gain, and like great bulls, they always long for the Dharma. They have transcended the realm of Māra and are not dependent on others; They meditate on the four concentrations, yet do not dwell within those concentrations.
examples.gm: Making themselves clean and wearing clean clothes, the three are isolated and pure; Without desire for gain, the supreme leaders always desire the dharma. Passed beyond the realm of Māra and not placing themselves under the control of others, Meditating on the four dhyānas, they do not abide in those dhyānas.
examples.sa: शुचिशौचअम्बरधरा त्रिविवेकशुद्धा न च लाभकाम वृषभा सद धर्मकामाः । मारस्यतीतविषया अपरप्रणेया चतुध्यानध्यायि न च निश्रित तत्र ध्याने ॥

examples.dm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles Might remain in the sky and simultaneously display various transformations; He demonstrates walking, moving, lying down, and sitting, And he does not grow weary, nor does he become exhausted.
examples.gm: For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles, Abiding in space, simultaneously emanates magical creations, Demonstrating walking, pacing, sleeping, and sitting; He has no weariness, and he has no fatigue.
examples.sa: भिक्षू यथा परमऋद्धिबलेनुपेतो गगने स्थितो यमक कुर्वति प्रातिहार्यां । गतिचंक्रमं शयनिषद्य निदर्शयाति न निवर्तते न पि च खिद्यति याव तत्र ॥

examples.dm: Except for those who constantly dwell in villages, regions, and towns, Striving for awakening and the ripening of sentient beings, And who do not generate the desire for the state of an Arhat or Pratyekabuddha— This is what the Sugata calls the solitude of the [Buddha's] sons.
examples.gm: Constantly abiding in villages, provinces, and towns, Except for striving for awakening to mature sentient beings, They do not produce other desires for arhatship or pratyekabuddhahood; This is taught by the sons of the Sugata as being solitary.
examples.sa: ग्रामे च राष्ट्रि निगमे विहरन्ति नित्यं रहप्रत्ययानि स्पृहतां जनयन्ति तत्र । अन्यत्र सत्त्वपरिपाचनबोधियुक्ता एषो विवेकु कथितो सुगतात्मजानाम् ॥

examples.dm: Sentient beings, completely famished, desire food, And those with minds attached to cyclic existence wander perpetually. The two phenomena of "self" and "mine" are unreal and empty; Yet the foolish, by their own doing, tie knots in the sky.
examples.gm: Fully starving sentient beings desire food, and Those possessing a mind attached to saṃsāra constantly wander. Both self and the phenomena of self are unreal and empty; Childish beings themselves have cast a knot in space.
examples.sa: आहारकाम परिकल्पयमान सत्त्वाः संसारि युक्तमनसः सद संस्मरन्ति । अहु मह्य धर्म उभि एति अभूत शून्या आकाशगण्ठि अयु आत्मन बद्ध बाले ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the bodhisattva who practices the supreme perfection of wisdom, Dwelling in emptiness and the signless, Having destroyed the dense darkness of views, outshines all worldly beings, Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, and the many bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: Just so, the bodhisattva practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, Practicing emptiness and signlessness, The wise one, having destroyed the dense thicket of views, outshines all beings, Arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and many bodhisattvas.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितां चरन्तो विधमित्व दृष्टिगहनं विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । अभिभोन्ति सर्वजगती रहप्रत्ययांश्च शून्यानिमित्तचरितो पृथु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who understands this kind of training Will never again suffer a decline in training or become immoral; In order to please the Buddha-dharmas, they train in this, Skilled in the higher training, they train without apprehension.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva knows this training like that, Will never become one with degenerate training or faulty ethical discipline; In order to please the Buddhas, they train in this; They are wise in the higher training and lack apprehension.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व इमु जानति एव शिक्षां न स जातु शिक्षविकलो भवते दुशीलो । आराधितेषु इह शिक्षति बुद्धधर्मं शिक्षातिशिक्षकुशलो ति निरूपलम्भो ॥

examples.dm: I also rejoice in the mass of merit of all sentient beings, as many as there are, Who strive for virtue and desire to be of benefit; Therefore, once they have attained the qualities of the Victors, They bestow the gift of Dharma upon the world in order to bring suffering to an end.
examples.gm: Seeking virtue and desiring to benefit however many sentient beings there are, They also rejoice in the heaps of merit of them all; Therefore, having attained the qualities of the Victorious Ones, In order to exhaust suffering, they give the gift of Dharma to the world.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व कुशलार्थिक मोक्षकामा सर्वेष भोन्ति अनुमोदितु पुण्यराशि । सत्त्वर्थि ते जिनगुण अनन्त प्रापुणित्वा दास्यन्ति धर्म जगती दुखसंक्षयाये ॥

examples.dm: Through four causes, the wise and powerful bodhisattva Is difficult for the four Māras to overcome and cannot be shaken: Abiding in emptiness, never forsaking sentient beings, Acting exactly as one speaks, and possessing the blessings of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: By four causes, the wise bodhisattva possesses strength, Is hard to overcome by the four Māras, and cannot be moved: Dwelling in emptiness, not forsaking sentient beings, Acting as they have spoken, and possessing the blessing of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: चतुकारणेहि बलवां विदु बोधिसत्त्वो भवते दुघर्षु चतुमारअसंप्रकम्प्यो । शून्याविहारि भवते न च सत्त्वत्यागी यथवादि सत्त्वकरुणानुगतावस्थानः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who, regarding dependent origination, Understands this wisdom to be without birth and without exhaustion, Just as the cloudless sun dispels darkness by radiating its beams of light, Will, by destroying the dense gloom of ignorance, attain the self-arisen state.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva, with regard to dependent origination, Knows this wisdom as unborn and unexhausted, Just as the cloudless sun dispels darkness by emitting rays of light, Having destroyed dense ignorance, will attain the state of the Self-Arisen.
examples.sa: यो तु प्रतीत्यसमुत्पादु अनुद्भवाये इमु प्रज्ञ अक्षयत बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । सो सूर्य अभ्रपटले यथ मुक्तरश्मी विधमित्वविद्यपटलं भवते स्वयंभूः ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva, while dwelling in meditative absorption and concentration, Should generate a mind that desires the vehicle of the Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas, They have become uncomposed, agitated, and mentally distracted; The Buddha's qualities are completely lost, like a ferryman whose boat has been wrecked.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva abides in the samādhis of the dhyānas, But generates a mind desiring the vehicle of an arhat or pratyekabuddha, They are not in meditative equipoise, but agitated and their mind is distracted; The qualities of a Buddha completely diminish, like a boatman whose boat breaks.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व विहराति समाधिध्याने रहप्रत्ययानि स्पृहबुद्धि न संजनेय्या । असमाहितो भवति उद्धतक्षिप्तचित्तो परिहीनबुद्धिगुण नाविक भिन्ननावो ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who wishes to remain for a long time in cyclic existence, A yogi who perseveres in the welfare of sentient beings and the purification of the realm, If they do not give rise to even a speck of weariness, They possess the perfection of diligence and are never negligent.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva wishes to cycle in saṃsāra for a long time, A yogi exerting themselves for the benefit of sentient beings and purifying the realms, If they do not generate even an atom of a weary mind, They are endowed with the perfection of diligence and are free from idleness.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व चिरसंसरणाभिप्रायो सत्त्वार्थ क्षेत्रपरिशोधनयुक्तयोगी । न च खेदबुद्धि अणुमात्र उपादियाति सो वीर्यपारमितयुक्त अतन्द्रितश् च ॥

examples.dm: If some being were to take a sachet of sandalwood powder And, with great devotion, apply it to a bodhisattva, While another person sprinkles glowing embers over his head, He should generate a mind that is equal and impartial toward both.
examples.gm: If some sentient being takes a handful of sandalwood And with great respect rubs it on the bodhisattva, While another scatters burning coals on their head, towards both They should generate an equal and even mind.
examples.sa: सचि कश्चि चन्दनपुटं ग्रहियान सत्त्वो अभ्योकिरेय गुरुप्रेमत बोधिसत्त्वम् । द्वितीयोऽपि अग्नि सकले शिरसि क्षिपेया उभयत्र तुल्यु मनु तेन उपादितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
examples.gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.
examples.sa: यस्यो न अस्ति अहसंज्ञ न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविरागु कुतु तस्य असंवरोऽस्ति । यस्यो न संवरि असंवरि मन्यनास्ति अयु शीलसंवरु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are without exception throughout the three realms of existence, If one were to take all of them as a basis for consideration, and if all of them, To the Knowers of the World—the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas— Were to give gifts for infinite eons while seeking the excellence of a Śrāvaka,
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are without exception in the three states of existence, Taking them fully into consideration, if all of them To the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas Give gifts for infinite eons, and properly seek the śrāvaka path—
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व त्रिभवे निखिलेन अस्ति ते सर्वि दान ददयन्ति अनन्तकल्पान् । बुद्धानुलोकि विदु नार्हतिप्रत्ययानां यावन्ति श्रावकगुणान् परिकल्प स्थाने ॥

examples.dm: Through diligence, virtuous qualities will not decline; One will find the treasury of the Victors, which is infinite primordial wisdom. Through meditative concentration, one abandons the base qualities of sensual desire; One fully accomplishes knowledge, supernormal powers, and meditative absorption.
examples.gm: By diligence, pure qualities will not diminish, And infinite pristine wisdom, the treasury of the Victors, will be found. By concentration, the despised qualities of desire are discarded, And knowledge, superknowledges, and samadhi are accomplished.
examples.sa: वीर्येण शुक्लगुण हानि न अभ्युपैति ज्ञानं अनन्त लभते जिनकोशगञ्जम् । ध्यानेन कामगुण उत्सृजते जुगुप्स्यान् विद्या अभिज्ञ अभिनिर्हरते समाधिम् ॥

examples.dm: As the supreme physician who heals the ailments of wandering beings, He has spoken this teaching on wisdom, which possesses the path to enlightenment; This path to awakening is titled "The Collection of Precious Qualities," And is taught so that all sentient beings may attain it.
examples.gm: By the supreme physician who heals the diseases of beings, This teaching of wisdom, endowed with the path to awakening, was taught; Its name is the Collection of Precious Qualities, the path to awakening; This path was explained in order for all sentient beings to obtain it.
examples.sa: वैद्योत्तमो जगति रोगचिकित्सकारी प्रज्ञोपदेश कथितो अयु बोधिमार्गो । नामेन रत्नगुणसंचय बोधिमार्गः तं सर्वसत्त्व इतु मार्गतु प्राप्नुवन्ति ॥
